29 October 2026

Official advisory on blockade enforcement in the Strait of Hormuz with notice to avoid unnecessary transit

Threat Level
High

during the period 280400Z–290400Z October 2026, the threat level remained high in the Strait of Hormuz, the Arabian Gulf, the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab, and medium in the Arabian Sea and the eastern Mediterranean. An official advisory on blockade enforcement was issued with notice to avoid unnecessary transit, and an Iranian threat of retaliation was reported alongside a negotiating track to reopen the strait. Yemen reports focused on ports and civil aviation.

Event Log IMO and Confirmed Incidents

No new incident was entered in the International Maritime Organization register during the period. Therefore, no additional number was added to the register known from the previous report.

Events 29-05, 29-06, 29-07, 29-08, 29-09, 29-12 and 29-13 are not entered in the Confirmed Incidents register because their information is reported or professional and not officially confirmed. Events 29-14, 29-15 and 29-16 are land incidents, not maritime incidents.

Continuous Monitoring

We are tracking updates from UKMTO and JMIC and every navigational warning mentioning a vessel, location, or hazardous object in the separation scheme. UKMTO and JMIC, and every navigational warning mentioning a vessel, a location or a hazardous object in the traffic separation scheme.

We are monitoring any official announcement of reopening the Strait of Hormuz or changing transit conditions, and any field implementation of a reopening plan.

We are monitoring any questioning or inspection of a vessel in the Arabian Gulf or Gulf of Oman, and identifying the time, location, and entity.

We are monitoring reports of attacks on ports and civil aviation in the Gulf of Aden, and the status of medicine and oxygen stocks in Yemen.

Threat Level

Official assessment, analytical judgement, and confidence limits.

The threat level in the Strait of Hormuz and the Arabian Gulf: high. This assessment is based on the blockade-implementation advisory, the advice to avoid unnecessary transit, and an Iranian threat to respond to vessel escorts.

The threat level in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab: persistently high; its basis within the period is land-based targeting of ports and civil aviation in Aden and reports of shells in Taiz, with no new maritime event during the period. The assessment is persistent, not event-driven.

The threat level in the Arabian Sea: persistently medium; no new maritime event in the area appeared in the period’s materials, so this level is not based on an event within the period.

The threat level in the Eastern Mediterranean: persistently medium; the reviewed materials contained no new maritime event in the area.

Official warnings and advisories

Status of official parties during the reporting period.

What was announced by official bodies during the period: an advisory was issued JMIC No. 016-26 on the implementation of the blockade, issued by UKMTO on behalf of the Center.

An advisory notice was also issued by UKMTO No. 184-26 on reports of suspicious activity. The details of the advisory were not available on the page UKMTO official until 290303Z, and therefore its scope was not included in this report. No new navigational warning identifying a location or a hazardous object in the traffic separation scheme was issued during the period.

Probabilities and Attribution of Incidents to Entities

Who might be responsible — stated without assertion and without attribution without evidence.

The percentages below are estimates, collectively exhaustive, and total 100%. No percentage constitutes evidence confirming an executing entity.

  • 30% — Pressure on transit through the Strait of Hormuz continues: a blockade-enforcement notice was issued and transit was advised against.
  • 25% — Questioning or inspection of a neutral vessel occurs: the notice explicitly mentions questioning and inspection.
  • 20% — Targeting of ports and civil aviation in the Gulf of Aden continues: government and local reports recurred.
  • 15% — Announcement of reopening the Strait of Hormuz without immediate implementation: a seven-day plan proposal under review appeared.
  • 10% — Reports of vessels being struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz decline: no new official report was issued during the period.
